title: Visual Capture Evidence
description: Machine-readable record of what a visual benchmark capture ACTUALLY produced, as opposed to the GoldenSceneManifest which records what was requested. The evidence artifact is the fact layer: it never states whether an image is good. Enforced by tools/visual_benchmark/validate_capture_evidence.py. IMPORTANT: integration/render-v2 has no capture backend yet, so no artifact with capture_success=true can exist today; the contract ships first so the future runtime capture has a stable shape to fill. Unavailability policy: null is the ONLY marker for 'not available' - never 0, -1 or an empty string, which is why every dimension and byte size has a minimum of 1. Presence policy: every property of every object is listed in that object's `required` array, so a leaf must always be PRESENT - either with a real value or with an explicit null. An omitted key is an incomplete, non-conforming artifact and is never equivalent to null, because null is the producer stating it followed the contract while absence means it did not.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this evidence contract. The validator accepts major version 1 only.

scene_id.description: Scene this evidence describes. Must equal the scene_id of the manifest that was run; the validator cross-checks it when --manifest is supplied.

path.description: Manifest path as seen by the producer, when applicable. null when the producer has no meaningful path to report.

path_display.description: Repo-relative display path, matching the runner's display_path convention. null when not applicable.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact manifest bytes that were run. Mandatory and never null: without it the evidence cannot be tied to an intent, and the validator rejects a digest that does not match the supplied manifest file.

manifest.description: Provenance of the GoldenSceneManifest this evidence was produced from.

commit_sha.description: Full git commit SHA the capture was produced from. 40 hex for SHA-1 repositories, 64 for SHA-256 ones.

commit_sha_short.description: Short commit SHA for human reading. null when git is unavailable.

branch.description: Branch name. Legitimately null on a detached HEAD or when git is unavailable.

detached_head.description: True when the commit was checked out without a branch. null when git is unavailable.

dirty.description: True when the work tree had uncommitted changes, which makes the commit SHA an incomplete description of what ran. null when git is unavailable.

dirty_entry_count.description: Number of `git status --porcelain` entries. null when git is unavailable.

source.description: Where the produced bytes came from. Tooling-supplied.

version.description: Renderer backend that produced the frame.

exposure_ev.description: Exposure in EV stops actually in effect.

renderer.description: Renderer state recorded as fact. Every leaf is nullable so a producer that cannot report a value says so instead of guessing. Tooling-supplied from the manifest until the runtime can confirm it.

frame_index.description: Presentation frame index the manifest asked to capture. null when the manifest omits capture.frame.

requested.description: Intent, copied from the manifest. Tooling-supplied.

framebuffer_width.description: REAL framebuffer width the runtime presented. null until a capture backend reports it. Minimum 1 so 0 can never pose as 'unavailable'.

framebuffer_height.description: REAL framebuffer height the runtime presented. null until a capture backend reports it.

presentation_frame_index.description: REAL presentation frame index the image was taken from. null until a capture backend reports it.

actual.description: What the runtime really produced. Kept in a separate object from `requested` so a divergence - for example the current hardcoded 1280x720 window against a requested 1920x1080 - stays visible instead of being overwritten. Runtime-supplied (LINEA 1 handshake).

format.description: Image format the artifact is written in.

path.description: Where the image was written. null when no image exists.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the image bytes. null when no image exists. Mandatory when execution.capture_success is true.

byte_size.description: Image size in bytes. null when no image exists; minimum 1 so a placeholder 0 is rejected.

image.description: The image artifact itself. Runtime-supplied (LINEA 1 handshake). All three leaves are mandatory when capture_success is true and must all be null when it is false.

capture.description: Requested intent versus actual result, kept structurally distinct.

capture_success.description: FACT: an image artifact was really produced. This is a procedural statement only. It is NOT visual_pass and must never be read as an approval of image quality.

process_exit_code.description: Exit code of the capture process. null when no process ran. Must be 0 or null when capture_success is true.

failure_reason.description: Why nothing was captured. Mandatory when capture_success is false, and must be null when it is true.

gpu_adapter_name.description: wgpu adapter name, ONLY if the runtime really reports it. null otherwise - never guessed. Runtime-supplied.

graphics_backend.description: Graphics backend (vulkan/dx12/metal/gl), ONLY if really reported. null otherwise. Runtime-supplied.

driver_version.description: Driver or adapter driver version, ONLY if really reported. null otherwise. Runtime-supplied.

notes.description: Free text for provenance caveats, e.g. why a field is unavailable.

hardware.description: Hardware and driver provenance. An all-null block is valid and honest: it states that nothing was reported, which is different from claiming known hardware.

visual_pass.description: MUST be present and MUST be null in v1. Capture evidence records facts and never a visual verdict: no SSIM/PSNR/LPIPS threshold and no automatic PASS/FAIL exists in this repository. Omitting the key is rejected - leaving the verdict open is not the same as declaring it null. The field is present so a future approved reviewer or metrics engine has a reserved, versioned home, and so any producer that fills it today fails validation.

visual_pass_reason.description: Why visual_pass is null. Keeps the absence explicit rather than silent.

verdict.description: Visual verdict. Locked to null in v1 - evidence is not approval.
